items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:67:1
items.html:
So is AA of the male to Atik of the male, just as Israel Saba to Aba, and just as Yaakov to ZA, etc.: This is yet another thing drawn from Nekudim, where the bottom Hey rose into the Einayim and the AHP of every degree came out to the discernment of the one lower than it. And therefore every lower one is considered half of the lower degree of its upper one, that is, the AHP of the upper one. Hence the Rosh of Atzilut, namely the Keter, was divided into two degrees, GE and AHP. These are Atik and AA. Likewise, the Toch of Atzilut was divided into GE and AHP, which are AVI and YESHSUT. And likewise the Sof of Atzilut was divided into GE and AHP, which are ZA and the upper Rachel, and Yaakov and the lower Rachel. Now, the GE are the discernments of the GAR [first three] of the degree, which are its KHB, for the Einayim and the Nikvey Einayim include Hochma and the GAR of Bina. And the AHP that came out outside the degree include the seven lower ones of Bina and ZON.
The reason for this division in the middle of Bina is that the bottom Hey rose into the Einayim, which is Hochma, and brought the AHP out to the outside. Since they are below the screen that is included in the restricted bottom Hey, this restriction that is in the bottom Hey cannot rule over the GAR of Bina so as to remove them on this account from the category of Rosh. For the entire matter of the restriction is only over the light of Hochma. And the GAR of Bina, in any case, do not receive the light of Hochma, but only the light of Hassadim, in the secret of “for He desires kindness.” And therefore the GAR of Bina never go out of the degree, because the bottom Hey rose above them. And for this reason it is regarded that the Sefira of Bina was divided in two: her GAR remained in the upper degree, that is, with the GE, while her seven lower ones descended with ZON to the lower degree. For the seven lower ones of Bina need the illumination of Hochma, and therefore the power of the restriction in the bottom Hey already rules over them. And therefore they resemble ZON.
And with this you will understand why all the levels that came out of MA are complete. Only the level of Bina of MA was separated into two: the GAR of Bina of MA were taken by the upper AVI, and the seven lower ones of Bina of MA were taken by YESHSUT. Not so the Keter of MA, which was taken by Atik, with all the ten Sefirot within it; so too, Hochma of MA was taken by AA; and ZA of MA was taken by ZA; and Malchut of MA was taken by Malchut. Thus, no Sefira of MA was separated into two halves; rather, the lower Sefira is considered the AHP of the upper Sefira: Hochma of MA became the AHP of the Keter, and Malchut of MA became the AHP of the ZA of MA. But in every one of them, all the ten Sefirot in the Sefira remained united in their completeness. Only Bina of MA alone was separated into two halves: the GAR for AVI and the seven lower ones for YESHSUT.
And from the above you will understand this well, for all five Partzufim of Atzilut are considered, in their entirety, as one degree that has ten Sefirot in it. Therefore the entirety, too, must necessarily be divided into GE and AHP, like the particulars. As is known, the particulars and the whole are always equal to one another. And therefore the GE of Atzilut include the GAR, namely:
Keter, Hochma and the GAR of Bina. And the AHP of the whole of Atzilut include the seven lower ones of Bina, ZA and Malchut. Such that from the Chazeh [chest] of AA and upward, it is the discernment of the Galgalta, Einayim and Nikvey Einayim of the whole, which are Atik, AA and the upper AVI. And from the Chazeh of AA and downward, it is the discernment of the AHP of the whole, which are YESHSUT, ZA and the Nukva. And with this you will understand the great advantage that the upper AVI have: although they clothe the body of AA from the throat to the Chazeh, they are still considered the discernment of the Rosh of Atzilut, because the screen rules over the GAR of Bina not at all, as above. And remember this.

items.html: Three aspects of male and female, namely: one, Atik and Nukva, in which AA and Nukva are included; two, AVI, in which YESHSUT are included, etc.: They are the root of the Mochin, the Mochin themselves, and the receivers of the Mochin, as above (page 630, the passage beginning “And All”), study it there well. The continuation of the ARI’s words will be explained in the Inner Observation here.
